turns.prompt_text: Alrighty, I would like to create an SCAD On 3D model. That's because I would like to print an eyedrop funnel. I have a small eyedrop funnel with a 5 mm diameter outer nozzle, base. I would like to create a small funnel so that I can refill it.
turns.response_html:
Alrighty! Making a custom funnel is a perfect job for OpenSCAD and 3D printing. Since you're dealing with a tiny 5 mm outer nozzle, the best approach is to design a funnel with a "sleeve" that slides securely over the outside of that nozzle, rather than trying to balance a tiny spout inside of it.

Here is a clean, fully parametric OpenSCAD script to generate your funnel.

The OpenSCAD Code

You can copy and paste this directly into a new OpenSCAD file:

// Tiny Eyedrop Refill Funnel
// All units are in millimeters

$fn = 100; // High resolution for smooth, watertight curves

// --- Parameters ---
// Adjust these if your measurements need tweaking!
nozzle_outer_dia = 5.0;     // The 5mm outer diameter of your eyedropper base
tolerance = 0.4;            // Extra clearance so it slips over the nozzle easily
sleeve_height = 6.0;        // How far down the funnel grabs the bottle nozzle
funnel_top_dia = 20.0;      // Diameter of the wide, top pouring section
funnel_height = 15.0;       // How tall the actual conical part is
wall_thickness = 1.6;       // 1.6mm is 4 perimeters on a standard 0.4mm nozzle

// --- Calculated Values ---
inner_sleeve_dia = nozzle_outer_dia + tolerance;
outer_sleeve_dia = inner_sleeve_dia + (wall_thickness * 2);
outer_funnel_dia = funnel_top_dia + (wall_thickness * 2);

// --- 3D Model Generation ---
union() {
    // 1. The Top Conical Funnel
    translate([0, 0, sleeve_height])
    difference() {
        // Outer solid cone
        cylinder(h = funnel_height, d1 = outer_sleeve_dia, d2 = outer_funnel_dia);
        
        // Inner hollow cone
        translate([0, 0, -0.1])
        cylinder(h = funnel_height + 0.2, d1 = inner_sleeve_dia, d2 = funnel_top_dia);
    }

    // 2. The Bottom Sleeve (fits over your bottle's 5mm nozzle)
    difference() {
        // Outer solid cylinder
        cylinder(h = sleeve_height, d = outer_sleeve_dia);
        
        // Inner hollow cylinder
        translate([0, 0, -0.1])
        cylinder(h = sleeve_height + 0.2, d = inner_sleeve_dia);
    }
}

How to Tweak It

I made the code fully parametric, meaning you only need to change the numbers at the very top of the script to adjust the whole model:

  • tolerance = 0.4; This adds a 0.4 mm gap so the plastic doesn't fuse tightly to the bottle. If the print turns out too loose, drop this to 0.2. If it won't fit over the nozzle, bump it to 0.6.
  • funnel_top_dia = 20.0; This gives you a nice 2 cm wide target to pour into. You can make this wider if your liquid is tough to pour.

Quick Slicing Tips

When you load the exported STL into Bambu Studio to send over to your A1, keep these settings in mind for small, functional parts:

  • Layer Height: Drop this down to 0.12 mm or 0.08 mm. Because the funnel walls are sloped, smaller layer heights will make the inside surface much smoother, meaning your liquid won't get caught on the layer lines.
  • Wall Loops: Set your wall loops/perimeters to at least 3 or 4. You want this to be 100% watertight so nothing leaks through the sides.
  • Material: PETG or PLA both work great, though PETG is usually a bit more chemical resistant depending on what you are putting in the dropper.
